second_order: rallying people to help the cause
theme_note: These codes all recruit or promise people and outside help for a shared build; what varies is whether the appeal is for a first build, allies, reinforcements, or a last push.

second_order: supplying coordinates, templates and faster ways to place
theme_note: These codes make participation practicable by explaining the wait, locating the work, sharing a drawing, using extra accounts, proposing scripts or synchronized pixels, and even rehearsing offline.

second_order: finishing one picture and starting the next job
theme_note: These codes report visible progress or completion and turn it into another concrete task; the objects vary from the burgha and face to the logo, rainbow and LOOT GET!.

second_order: taking shifts to protect and repair the pictures
theme_note: These codes hold together as upkeep after a picture exists: ending a protection shift, assigning defenders, inviting more protection, defending from the void, warning about encroachment, repairing damage, and thanking protectors.

second_order: getting erased, blocked and cut off
theme_note: These codes describe pressure on the projects and make sense of losses; the pressure ranges from named groups and the void to overlapping flags, while responses vary from warning and apology to mourning, blame and admitting greed.

second_order: moving the face and switching to the J
theme_note: These codes all abandon, question or redirect a build when the current location stops working; what varies is who recommends the move, whether it is tentative, and whether the destination is another face or the smaller Jerma J.

second_order: asking permission and working out overlaps
theme_note: These exchanges negotiate who may occupy shared pixels. They range from checking an overlap and trading help to deals with neighbours, disputed spokespeople, permission from diplomats, and redesigning around a border or another drawing.

second_order: sending decisions and disputes through Discord
theme_note: These codes move coordination away from refreshing Reddit threads: people ask for the invite, report Discord rulings, and send contested-space questions there. What returns is a decision or direction, while much of the discussion remains unseen.

second_order: celebrating that Jerma made the final canvas
theme_note: These post-event codes jointly claim the outcome as a shared achievement, varying only in whether they name representation, congratulate everyone, or say the room made the big time.
